name: oneAPI DPC++ Compiler release 7.1.1
body:
## Components included in the release

- clang version `22.1.0`
- SYCL runtime version `9.0.0` (as indicated by predefined macro  `__LIBSYCL_MAJOR_VERSION`, `__LIBSYCL_MINOR_VERSION` and  `__LIBSYCL_PATCH_VERSION`)

## Compatibility with previous releases

This release is compatible with the previous v7.* releases.
Any applications built with these releases should continue to work with runtime shipped in this release.

## Compatibility with oneAPI

[Intel(R) oneAPI DPC++/C++ Compiler][oneapi-dpcpp] version 2026.1 release leverages codebase from the `sycl-rel-7_1` branch and it is the closest oneAPI DPC++/C++ compiler release to this one (in terms of available features and bugfixes).

**However**, this **does not** guarantee any feature or bugfix parity between these two releases.

## Validation & quality expectations

In general, list of supported hardware and operating systems should match the one provided by Intel(R) oneAPI DPC++/C++ Compiler for version 2026.1, see corresponding [system requirements][oneapi-dpcpp-system-reqs].

However, we **did not** perform the same exhaustive testing of this open-source branch and therefore there could be some unique issues that are not present in Intel (R) oneAPI DPC++/C++ Compiler version 2026.1.

You can find full validation logs for the branch [here](https://github.com/intel/llvm/actions/runs/34962479496) but a summary of it will also be posted below.

### [End to end tests][sycl-e2e]

The following hardware and software configurations were tested:

Driver versions listed as reported by `sycl::device::get_info<info::device::driver_version>()`.

- Windows
  - Intel(R) oneAPI Unified Runtime over Level-Zero on
    Intel(R) Iris(R) Xe Graphics 12.0.0
    - Driver version: [1.6.34728](https://www.intel.com/content/www/us/en/download/785597/intel-arc-iris-xe-graphics-windows.html)
  - Intel(R) oneAPI Unified Runtime over Level-Zero on
    Intel(R) Arc(TM) A770 Graphics
    - Driver version: [1.15.38308](https://www.intel.com/content/www/us/en/download/785597/intel-arc-iris-xe-graphics-windows.html)
  - Intel(R) oneAPI Unified Runtime over Level-Zero on
    Intel(R) Arc(TM) B580 Graphics 20.1.0
    - Driver version: [1.15.38308](https://www.intel.com/content/www/us/en/download/785597/intel-arc-iris-xe-graphics-windows.html)

- Linux (Ubuntu 22.04)
  - Intel(R) OpenCL Graphics on Intel(R) Iris(R) Xe Graphics
    - Driver version: [26.18.38308.1](https://github.com/intel/compute-runtime/releases/tag/26.18.38308.1)
  - Intel(R) oneAPI Unified Runtime over Level-Zero on
    Intel(R) Iris(R) Xe Graphics 12.0.0
    - Driver version: [1.15.38308+1](https://github.com/intel/compute-runtime/releases/tag/26.18.38308.1)
  - Intel(R) oneAPI Unified Runtime over Level-Zero on
    Intel(R) Arc(TM) B580 Graphics 20.1.0
    - Driver version: [1.15.38308+1](https://github.com/intel/compute-runtime/releases/tag/26.18.38308.1)
  - Intel(R) oneAPI Unified Runtime over Level-Zero on
    Intel(R) Arc(TM) A750 Graphics
    - Driver version: [1.15.38308+1](https://github.com/intel/compute-runtime/releases/tag/26.18.38308.1)
  - Intel(R) OpenCL on
    11th Gen Intel(R) Core(TM) i7-1165G7 @ 2.80 Ghz OpenCL 3.0
    - Driver version: [2026.21.3.0.31_160000](https://github.com/intel/llvm/releases/tag/2026-WW22)
  - NVIDIA CUDA BACKEND on NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3090
    - Driver version: CUDA 12.7

### [SYCL CTS][sycl-cts]

Please note that releases made from `intel/llvm` did not pass the formal [Conformance Process](https://www.khronos.org/conformance/adopters/) defined by the Khronos Group and as such cannot be considered to be fully conformant or fully implementing the SYCL 2020 specification.

- Linux (Ubuntu 22.04)
  - Intel(R) OpenCL on
    11th Gen Intel(R) Core(TM) i7-1165G7 @ 2.80 Ghz OpenCL 3.0
    - Driver version: [2026.21.3.0.31_160000](https://github.com/intel/llvm/releases/tag/2026-WW22)
  - Intel(R) oneAPI Unified Runtime over Level-Zero on
    Intel(R) Iris(R) Xe Graphics 12.0.0
    - Driver version: [1.15.38308+1](https://github.com/intel/compute-runtime/releases/tag/26.18.38308.1)
- Windows
  - Intel(R) oneAPI Unified Runtime over Level-Zero on
    Intel(R) Iris(R) Xe Graphics 12.0.0
    - Driver version: [1.15.38308](https://www.intel.com/content/www/us/en/download/785597/intel-arc-iris-xe-graphics-windows.html)

We used [`493fca2e1f319516c0e9816cd4a714c9c37f1220`](https://github.com/KhronosGroup/SYCL-CTS/tree/493fca2e1f319516c0e9816cd4a714c9c37f1220) CTS in our validation.

## How to use

Pre-built binaries are provided for Windows & Linux. Archives contain both SYCL compiler and runtime files.
To use, unpack those and setup `PATH` & `LD_LIBRARY_PATH`/`PATH` & `LIB` env variables in accordance with
[Get Started Guide](https://github.com/intel/llvm/blob/sycl-rel-7_1/sycl/doc/GetStartedGuide.md#run-simple-dpc-application).

Binaries were built using the following project configuration (below is an (incomplete) list of (key) arguments passed to `buildbot/configure.py` script):
```
# Linux:
-t Release --use-zstd --ci-defaults --disable-jit --no-assertions --add_security_flags=sanitize --hip --cuda
# Windows:
--ci-defaults --use-zstd --disable-jit --no-assertions --add_security_flags=sanitize
```

As you can see, SYCL JIT library is not being built, OpenMP is not being built, HIP & CUDA plugins on Windows are not being built.
If you are interested in a different configuration, you will have to build it yourself. To do so, follow
[Get Started Guide](https://github.com/intel/llvm/blob/sycl-rel-7_1/sycl/doc/GetStartedGuide.md)

[oneapi-dpcpp]: https://www.intel.com/content/www/us/en/developer/tools/oneapi/dpc-compiler.html
[oneapi-dpcpp-system-reqs]: https://www.intel.com/content/www/us/en/developer/articles/system-requirements/intel-oneapi-dpcpp-system-requirements.html
[sycl-e2e]: https://github.com/intel/llvm/tree/sycl-rel-7_1/sycl/test-e2e
[sycl-cts]: https://github.com/KhronosGroup/SYCL-CTS

## What's Changed

- Restricted host tasks (`sycl::ext::oneapi::experimental::host_task`) can now be captured while SYCL Graph native recording mode is active
- Added `command_graph::get_id()` to query a process-unique graph ID during SYCL Graph recording

**Full Changelog**: https://github.com/intel/llvm/compare/v7.1.0...v7.1.1
